why: Accessibility rule 1: primary text and icons reach 4.5:1 on every tone
Accessibility rule 1: dim text reaches 4.5:1 on every tone
Accessibility rule 2: accent reaches 3:1 against every tone it marks (check marks, block markers, fills on tracks)
Accessibility rule 1: on-accent text reaches 4.5:1 on accent
Accessibility rule 2: a hovered or focused checked toggle is filled with accent hover, which reaches 3:1 against the surface it marks
Accessibility rule 1: on-danger text and icons reach 4.5:1 on danger; text on danger does not
Accessibility rule 5: the window outline tells a window from the one behind it. 1.3 is provisional until O-4 sets the minimum.
Accessibility rule 5: the window glow marks the active window. 1.3 is provisional until O-4 sets the minimum.
Accessibility rule 4: the focused tone stands apart from the widget at rest and from the surface. 1.2 is provisional until O-3 sets the minimum.
Accessibility rule 4: the focused tone stands apart from the widget at rest and from the surface. 1.2 is provisional until O-3 sets the minimum.
Accessibility, departure from WCAG: an empty well is told from its surface by tone. 1.1 is provisional until O-1 sets the minimum.
Accessibility, departure from WCAG: an empty well is told from its surface by tone. 1.1 is provisional until O-1 sets the minimum.
Accessibility, departure from WCAG: an unchecked toggle is told from its surface by tone. 1.1 is provisional until O-1 sets the minimum.
Accessibility rule 4: the focused tone stands apart from the widget at rest and from the surface. 1.2 is provisional until O-3 sets the minimum.
Accessibility, departure from WCAG: an empty track is told from its surface by tone. 1.1 is provisional until O-1 sets the minimum.
Accessibility, departure from WCAG: a scrollbar's thumb is told from its surface by tone. 1.1 is provisional until O-1 sets the minimum.
A selected item is grouped by tone; its block marker carries rule 2's 3:1. 1.1 is a floor that keeps the tone from fading (my call).
